title: Masking in PTGui Pro: painting, filling, and transferring masks across source images
summary: This PTGui tutorial explains masking as a Pro-level feature that defines which pixels from source images participate in the final panorama. It demonstrates selecting two overlapped images, using Edit Mask to isolate a specific area (a logo) so it is either fully included or excluded, and viewing seam placement with Show Seams. The video then covers painting the mask with red (exclude), green (include), and erase, plus using the fill tool and polygon drawing to quick-fill regions. It shows how masking affects seam position, how to zoom and adjust pencil size, and how to link/unlink images for synchronized masking. Finally, it demonstrates transferring masks between images, copying and pasting masks across multiple images, and saving/loading mask files for reuse. The examples center on how masking can remove a logo from a panorama and how the same mask can be applied consistently across a set of images.

sections.description: An example uses a logo placed in one image within the overlapping region. The presenter right-clicks the area of interest, selects the two images, and chooses Edit Mask to switch to the Mask tab, preparing to adjust how the logo is treated in the blend.

sections.description: The video demonstrates linking image panels for synchronized masking, transferring masks between images, and copying/pasting masks across multiple images. It also shows how to save a mask to a file and load it into another project, which is useful for masking elements that appear identically (e.g., tripod) across frames.
